reason: The sole cited evidence (E1) demonstrates TiO precipitate formation and strength enhancement in a different alloy (NbMoTaWVTi) at room temperature, but provides no data on high-temperature strength, no support for the specific oxygen doping range, and no evidence that the mechanism applies to TiVNbTa or at 1273 K. The key premises about elevated-temperature strengthening and applicability to TiVNbTa are therefore unsupported by the cited passage.
premises: TiO precipitates can form in a BCC refractory HEA matrix via mechanical alloying and spark plasma sintering
TiO precipitates act as obstacles to dislocation motion and hinder thermally activated recovery at high temperature
Controlled oxygen doping (~0.1–0.2 wt% O) during processing can yield a fine, homogeneous dispersion of TiO
Precipitation strengthening by TiO can significantly elevate yield strength at 1273 K (e.g., from ~330 MPa to >500 MPa)
The TiVNbTa alloy system is amenable to this approach without excessive embrittlement
